speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you tell me when the swelling and pain in your right ring finger started, and has it been getting worse gradually or suddenly?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: That mechanism of injury strongly suggests a tendon issue. Can you actively straighten the tip of your right ring finger, or does it remain stuck in a bent position?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text: The inability to actively flex the fingertip suggests an avulsion of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon, commonly known as a Jersey finger. Let's confirm the location of the injury by checking for a palpable gap or retracted tendon belly in the palm or finger; can you feel any tenderness or a lump along the palm side of your finger or palm?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Student and active in sports, particularly football. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Doctor
text: The mechanism of injury and your specific symptoms point strongly to a Jersey finger, which is an avulsion of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon. I need to visualize the tendon's position to confirm this, so I will order imaging. REQUEST TEST: Ultrasound_of_right_ring_finger

speaker: Doctor
text: The ultrasound results showing normal readings are unexpected given your inability to flex the fingertip, which strongly suggests a mechanical problem with the tendon.
